transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello. Um, well, occupational health actually sent me. I suppose it's because I’ve gotten into this pattern lately where... well, during my lab runs or exhibition work, I just push breakfast and lunch aside. I get busy and just work through. And then, by the time I actually do eat, I keep it to something very small and controlled.
Do you find yourself particularly concerned about your weight or the way your body looks when you're deciding what or how much to eat?

Yes, I am. I mean... I check my weight pretty carefully. If the scale goes up even a tiny fraction, I just feel this sharp panic. It's like I'm losing all the discipline I've worked so hard to maintain. So, yes, that definitely dictates why I keep my meals so small.
Do you ever make yourself sick, exercise excessively, or use laxatives or diuretics to control your weight or shape?

No, I don't do any of that. I don't make myself sick or take any pills like laxatives. And I don't really have the time or energy to exercise a lot, honestly. I just control my weight by strictly limiting what I eat.
Do you ever feel like you shouldn't eat because you believe your body is bigger or heavier than it actually is, even when others might not see it that way?

Yes, I suppose I do. When I look in the mirror before going to the lab, I don’t see someone thin. I mostly notice my stomach or my hips, and I just feel as if they make me look... careless, or unserious. It makes me feel like I need to keep restricting my food so I don't look that way.
